english: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all tangent lines to the curve $y=e^{x}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$. With $p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, the differential equation of $\mathcal{F}$, free of every arbitrary constant, is
hindi: माना कि $\mathcal{F}$ वक्र $y=e^{x}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$ की सभी स्पर्श रेखाओं का कुल है। $p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ लेने पर, $\mathcal{F}$ का प्रत्येक स्वेच्छ अचर से मुक्त अवकल समीकरण है
solution: Tangent at $(t,e^{t})$: $y-e^{t}=e^{t}(x-t)\Rightarrow y=e^{t}(x-t+1)$, a one-parameter family (parameter $t$)
(B) drops the $+1$ of $-t+1$; (D) has the sign of $p\ln p$ reversed
solution_full: The point of contact on $y=e^{x}$ is $(t,e^{t})$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and the slope there is $e^{t}$.

Tangent line: $y-e^{t}=e^{t}(x-t)$, that is, $y=e^{t}(x-t+1)$. Each member of $\mathcal{F}$ corresponds to one value of $t$, so the family has one arbitrary constant and its differential equation is of first order.
Differentiate the equation of the line with respect to $x$ (with $t$ fixed): $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{t}$, so $p=e^{t}$ and $t=\ln p$ (valid since $p>0$).
Substitute in the line: $y=p\left(x-\ln p+1\right)=p(x+1)-p\ln p$.
Check with the tangent at $t=0$: $y=x+1$, $p=1$, and $p(x+1)-p\ln p=x+1$, as required.
Option (B) comes from writing the tangent as $y=e^{t}(x-t)$; option (D) from a sign slip in $-pt=-p\ln p$; option (A) from using $x+t-1$.
originality_note: New: the differential equation of the family of all tangent lines of y = e^x (an envelope relation of d'Alembert type), obtained by eliminating the point of contact. Closest known: Clairaut equations for tangents of a parabola or circle. Different because: the slope parameter enters through a logarithm, so the result is not of Clairaut form y = px + g(p).
blueprint_concepts: Formation of a differential equation by eliminating arbitrary constants
Equation of a tangent to a curve

concept_use.Formation of a differential equation by: The family is written with its one parameter t (the abscissa of the point of contact) and the parameter is eliminated by differentiation.
concept_use.Equation of a tangent to a curve: The tangent to y = e^x at (t, e^t) is y = e^t(x - t + 1); this line is the member of the family.
